summary: Writes the fixed two-byte global word_5C692C over the two bytes at the end of the null-terminated string a1 (at a1[strlen(a1)], i.e. at the terminator position), returning 0. If a1 is null, returns -1 without writing. Invoked by results, standings, message-buffer, career-stats HTML and related UI writers to stamp a shared value onto the tail of name/text buffers.

local_names.a1: null-terminated string buffer whose terminator-position word is overwritten
local_names.word_5C692C: fixed two-byte global value written to the string tail

operations.description: Null guard: if the string pointer a1 is null, return -1 immediately without touching memory.
Compute the end of the string via strlen(a1) so the write lands at the terminator position a1[strlen(a1)].
Store the two-byte global word_5C692C at the computed position (*(WORD*)&a1[strlen(a1)] = word_5C692C), overwriting the terminator and the following byte with the fixed value.

Invoked by results, standings, message and HTML-writing paths including sub_469900, ResultsPageBuilder, StandingsDisplay, MessageNameBufferUpdate, sub_475150, sub_47C360, sub_47D800, DriverCareerStatsHTMLWriter and sub_47E0A0.

unresolved: The purpose and value of the fixed word global 0x005C692C are unknown; the overwrite lands on the NUL terminator (and the byte after it), which would normally break the string, so the caller must treat the buffer as a fixed-size field rather than a C string afterwards.
Whether the two bytes replace the terminator or are appended into reserved space depends on the caller's buffer layout, which is not evidenced in this packet.
Caller names are prelabel labels; their semantics are not evidenced here.
